subject: SLA baseline adjustment and monthly credit tradeoffs
body:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@solaero.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: SLA baseline adjustment and monthly credit tradeoffs

Ellen / SolAero team —

Thanks for the productive conversation last week. Attached is a concise draft (redwood_SLA_proposal_20270316.pdf) that reflects the standard template we use plus a couple of exception options we discussed. High-level proposal:

- Baseline uptime (hosted): 99.7% monthly
- Baseline uptime (Dedicated): 99.9% monthly
- Monthly service credit cap: 5% of monthly recurring charges (applies to aggregate credits)
- Maintenance carveouts: planned maintenance with 72-hour advance notice, standard carveout up to 8 hours/month
- Latency commitments: p95 inference latency target 250ms for dedicated deployments; hosted provided as best-effort with historical benchmarks attached

We heard SolAero wants a higher baseline and a lower cap on credits — I put forward the template numbers above because they balance predictability for both sides. If you need a higher baseline (99.9%) we typically require either a Dedicated deployment or a reserved capacity commitment to guarantee it without a substantial change to pricing.

Please review the attached and call out the specific clauses you want us to iterate on (availability percentage, monthly cap, maintenance carveouts, or latency SLOs). Happy to hop on a short call to iron this out.

Best,

Lauren Bishop

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@solaero.com>

Cc: SolAero Procurement <procurement@solaero.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:18:12 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline adjustment and monthly credit tradeoffs

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the quick send. A few items from our side: we need the baseline uptime across the board raised to 99.9% (not split by hosted/dedicated), and we would like the monthly credit cap lowered to 3%.

Specific asks:
- 99.9% uptime monthly (applies to the service as a whole)
- Monthly service credit cap 3%
- Maintenance carveouts limited to emergency fixes only; planned maintenance should be scheduled with a minimum 14-day window and handled in a way that doesn't count against availability if scheduled during the agreed window
- We also want a p95 latency commitment for hosted at 300ms with a remediation ladder if p95 exceeds 500ms for two consecutive months

We attached a short document (SolAero_SLA_ask.docx) that highlights the clauses we think are important. We're prepared to discuss tradeoffs — if higher uptime is conditional on a dedicated node pool or a 12‑month commit, we're open to that but need to understand the pricing delta.

Regards,

Ellen Park

Subject: Re: SLA baseline adjustment and monthly credit tradeoffs (internal)

Lauren — quick technical read on SolAero's ask: 99.9% across all deployments for multi‑region hosted delivery is achievable but will materially increase cost unless we either (a) reserve capacity for them, or (b) limit the SLA to a regional subset. Our internal estimate (attached) shows a +22–28% infra delta to hit 99.9% for the traffic profile SolAero shared.

Options I recommend we present as tradeoffs:
- Offer tiered uptime: hosted 99.85% / dedicated 99.95% (gives stronger guarantee for reserved capacity)
- Or agree to 99.9% but require a 12‑month reserved capacity commit (and an additional monthly fee to cover the uplift)
- Reduce monthly credit cap to 4% as a middle ground (solves some of their downside exposure without exposing us to higher cap risk)

Also: maintenance windows — 14 days' notice for planned maintenance is reasonable for large accounts; we should keep an 8‑hour standard monthly carveout for platform upgrades but allow negotiated exceptions for dedicated deployments.

Attachment: capacity_impact_estimate.xlsx

Ben
Director, Solutions Architecture
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline adjustment and monthly credit tradeoffs

Ellen —

Thanks for the clear asks and for the attached note. We discussed this with engineering and solutions (Ben looped in) and legal/sales (Marissa copied). To land in the middle and keep things operationally supportable for both sides, here is a counterproposal we can sign off quickly on:

- Tiered uptime: Hosted 99.85% monthly; Dedicated 99.95% monthly (if you require 99.9% specifically we can offer it for Dedicated with no price change — hosted at 99.9% requires reserved capacity)
- Monthly credit cap: 4% of monthly recurring charges (applies to combined credits across regions)
- Maintenance carveouts: Planned maintenance with minimum 14‑day notice will be excluded from availability if executed within an agreed maintenance window; platform upgrades limited to 8 hours/month for hosted unless otherwise negotiated for dedicated pools
- Latency: p95 target for Dedicated 250ms; hosted p95 target 300ms with a remediation ladder if p95 exceeds 500ms for two consecutive months (documented in the playbook)
- If SolAero elects a 12‑month reserved capacity commit for hosted traffic, we will provide a subsequent rider to upgrade hosted uptime to 99.9% without additional per‑token uplift

Attached are redlines (SLA_Redlines_20270318.pdf). If this looks acceptable, Marissa can produce an updated SOW and we can push to DocuSign (link below). Happy to set a 30‑minute call tomorrow to finalize.
